name: AKT2-related Familial Partial Lipodystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for AKT2-related Familial Partial Lipodystrophy

criteria.description: Regional loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue predominantly affecting limbs and trunk with relative fat accumulation in face and neck
Severe insulin resistance manifesting as early-onset diabetes mellitus or impaired glucose tolerance
Identification of pathogenic heterozygous mutation in the AKT2 gene
Elevated serum triglycerides often exceeding 500 mg/dL
Evidence of fatty liver on imaging or biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of partial lipodystrophy phenotype plus pathogenic AKT2 mutation with or without insulin resistance
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; clinical features may overlap with other lipodystrophies.

laboratory: Elevated fasting insulin and glucose levels indicating insulin resistance
Elevated liver enzymes in some cases
imaging: MRI or CT showing selective loss of subcutaneous fat in limbs and trunk
Ultrasound or MRI evidence of hepatic steatosis
other: Skin biopsy showing loss of adipocytes in affected areas (rarely performed)

distinguishingFeatures: Severe metabolic complications early in life
Mutations in AGPAT2 or BSCL2 genes
Fat loss predominantly in limbs and trunk with fat accumulation in face and neck
Onset typically in adolescence or early adulthood

redFlags: Rapid onset of severe insulin resistance in young adults
Marked regional fat loss with metabolic complications
Family history of similar fat distribution abnormalities and diabetes
references: Kadowaki T, et al. AKT2 mutations cause familial partial lipodystrophy. Nat Genet. 2011.
Orphanet: AKT2-related familial partial lipodystrophy. ORPHA:79085.
Garg A. Lipodystrophies. Am J Med. 2000.
